plain.li: [agree] I'll walk the wall with you before dark.
[agree,against] We'll start hauling stone for the wall in the morning.
[debate] Ask me again after the next one, if we're both standing.
[argue,for] Stay behind your wall, then, and listen to the rest of us fight.
[argue,against] Run at them, then, and we'll carry you back in.

warm.li: [agree] Keep your head down next time, for me.
[debate,against] If you go out to meet them, I'm coming with you.

cheerful.li: [agree] Next time they come, they'll wish they'd stayed home.
[debate] Whoever's right buys the other a drink after the next one.

gloomy.li: [agree] They'll come again, they always do.
[debate,against] Walls or no walls, someone won't walk away from the next one.

cold.li: [agree,for] Then we meet them before they reach the fields.
[debate] The next raid will show us which of us was right, at a price.

plain.li: [agree,for] They're doing their best, and that's more than most would.
[agree,against] I'll write it down so I don't forget it by the meeting.
[debate] Ask them yourself, they do answer, mostly.
[argue,for] You'd do worse in their seat, and you know it.
[argue,against] Keep bowing to them, then.

warm.li: [agree] I'll sit next to you at the meeting.
[debate,for] Give them one more season, for me.

cheerful.li: [agree] I'll bring something to eat to the next meeting, that'll soften them.
[argue,for] Stand for the council yourself, then, and see how easy it is.

gloomy.li: [debate] Whoever sits up there, it ends up the same.
[agree,for] They mean well, which is about all you can say for anyone.

cold.li: [debate,against] Their decisions are on record, so we'll judge them by those.
[argue] Raise it at a meeting or stop raising it.

plain.li: [agree,against] I'll see if there's any salt left in the stores.
[agree,for] Fill your bowl and say thank you, that's what I do.
[debate] Your stomach and mine will never agree.
[argue,for] Cook it yourself if you're so clever.
[argue,against] Keep your praise, I'll keep my complaints.

warm.li: [agree] Save me a seat at supper.
[debate,against] I'll ask the cook to try something new, nicely.

blunt.li: [agree,for] Hot and filling, that'll do me.
[argue] Stop picking at it and eat.

cheerful.li: [agree] Whoever finishes first gets the crust.
[debate,for] One day I'll do the cooking, and then you'll miss this.

gloomy.li: [agree,against] Same pot, same stew, same again tomorrow.
[debate] Hungry or picky, we all end up eating it.

cold.li: [debate] What it does for us matters more than how it tastes.
[argue,for] Complain to the cook, not to me.

plain.li: [agree] Right, there's a pile of hauling waiting for me.
[agree,against] I'll keep a quiet eye on who's slacking.
[debate] We'll compare blisters at supper.
[argue,for] Count your own hours before you count mine.
[argue,for] You see slackers everywhere because you go looking for them.

warm.li: [agree] Shout if you need a hand later.
[debate,for] Maybe they're just tired, give them a day.

cheerful.li: [agree] Race you through the afternoon jobs.
[argue] I'll work so hard you'll be embarrassed.

gloomy.li: [agree] There's always more, it never stops.
[debate,against] They'll slack whatever we say.

cold.li: [debate] What gets done will settle it.
[agree,against] I'll note who's missing from their work.

plain.li: [agree,for] I'll ask {SUBJECT} to sit with us at supper.
[agree,against] I'll keep {SUBJECT} where I can see them.
[debate] {SUBJECT} will show us soon enough, one way or the other.
[argue,for] You were new here once too, remember.
[argue,against] Lend {SUBJECT} your tools, then, and see if you get them back.

warm.li: [agree] Let's make {SUBJECT} feel at home.
[debate,for] Give {SUBJECT} a chance, that's all I ask.

cheerful.li: [agree,for] I'm teaching {SUBJECT} the card game tonight.
[debate] A week of my cooking will show us what {SUBJECT} is made of.

gloomy.li: [agree] They come and they go, the new ones.
[debate,against] Don't get too fond, they don't always stay.

cold.li: [debate] We'll know {SUBJECT} by what gets done, not by what gets said.
[agree,for] {SUBJECT} is useful, and that's enough for me.

plain.li: [agree,for] There'll be a wedding before the year's out, you'll see.
[agree,against] Better a quiet bed than a broken heart.
[debate] Ask me again when it's your own heart.
[argue,for] You'll fall for someone one day, and I'll laugh.
[argue,against] Go and moon at someone, then.

warm.li: [agree] I hope you find someone who deserves you.
[debate,for] Hearts aren't all trouble, you know.

blunt.li: [argue] Keep your nose out of other people's hearts.

cheerful.li: [agree,for] I'll pick the flowers for the next wedding.
[debate] I'll make you blush yet, just you wait.

gloomy.li: [agree] Somebody always ends up crying.
[debate,against] Love's lovely until it isn't.

cold.li: [debate] Pairings keep people settled, that's all I'll grant.
[agree,against] Fewer couples, fewer quarrels.

plain.li: [agree,for] We'll make it a place they'd want to stay.
[agree,against,!nochildren] I'll keep them away from the gate when there's trouble.
[debate] We each had our own childhood, I suppose.
[argue,for] Children grow up anywhere, and they'll grow up here.
[argue,against] Keep telling yourself it's safe.

warm.li: [agree,!nochildren] I'll teach them their letters when the work's slack.
[debate,for] They'll be all right as long as we're around.

blunt.li: [agree,!nochildren] Watch the little ones, that's all.

cheerful.li: [agree,!nochildren] I'll show them how to skip stones.
[debate,for] Give a child a puddle and they're happy anywhere.

gloomy.li: [agree,against] I wouldn't bring a child here, not now.
[debate,!nochildren] They'll see things here no child should.

cold.li: [debate] What they learn here will keep them alive.
[agree,for,!nochildren] They're learning useful things, at least.

plain.li: [agree,for] I'll say their names at supper.
[agree,against] Let's leave them in peace.
[debate] Some days I want to talk about them, and some days I can't.
[argue,for] Forget them if you like, I won't.
[argue,against] Digging it all up again won't bring them back.

warm.li: [agree] Thank you for remembering them with me.
[debate,against] I'll keep them in my own heart, then, without the fuss.

cheerful.li: [agree,for] I still laugh at their stories, every time.
[debate] They'd have had something to say about this argument.

gloomy.li: [agree] Every one of them took something with them.
[debate,against] Remembering hurts, and so does forgetting.

cold.li: [debate] The living have work to do.
[agree,for] Their names are kept, I've made sure of it.

plain.li: [agree,for] I'll bring them a proper blanket.
[agree,against] I'll check the cell doors before bed.
[debate] They're people, and they're dangerous, and both are true.
[argue,for] Lock up your own heart while you're at it.
[argue,against] Feed them cake, then, and see what happens.

warm.li: [agree] Let's see they're fed and warm, whatever else.
[debate,for] Kindness costs us nothing, though.

blunt.li: [argue,against] Be soft with them and one of them will walk out the door.

cheerful.li: [agree,for] I'll teach them a song, it might cheer them up.
[debate] Careful, or they'll talk you into joining them.

gloomy.li: [agree] Those cells don't make anyone better.
[debate,for] Kind or not, they'll hate us for the bars.

cold.li: [debate] We treat them by what they're worth to us.
[agree,against] Plain food and hard work, until they join or go.

plain.li: [agree,for] One cup at supper never hurt anyone.
[agree,against] Water for me, and I'll sleep better for it.
[debate] We'll see who has the sore head in the morning.
[argue,for] More beer for the rest of us, then.
[argue,against] Drink yourself under the table, then.

warm.li: [agree] Let's look out for each other at the next feast.
[debate,for] Just the one, and then home to bed.

cheerful.li: [agree,for] To your health, and mine.
[debate] Loser drinks water for a week.

gloomy.li: [agree,against] I've seen it take people, and they don't come back from it.
[debate] We all lean on something.

cold.li: [debate] Some people can take it and some can't, that's all there is to it.
[agree,for] In measured amounts it keeps spirits up.

plain.li: [agree,for] I'll ask what they've been studying lately.
[agree,against] Old tools don't let you down when you need them.
[debate] We'll use whatever works, in the end.
[argue,for] Keep your old ways, then, and see who's still at it next winter.
[argue,against] Tinker away, and we'll see what breaks.

warm.li: [agree] I'll learn it if you teach me.
[debate,against] Show me the new way slowly, and I'll try it.

blunt.li: [agree,for] Learn it or get left behind.

cheerful.li: [agree,for] I can't wait to see what they come up with next.
[debate] Old way against new way, and we'll race to the finish.

gloomy.li: [agree,against] All this learning, and we still freeze in winter.
[debate] New or old, something always breaks.

cold.li: [debate] Whatever gets the work done faster wins.
[agree,for] Study comes first, then.

plain.li: [agree,for] I'll go and give them a brush before dark.
[agree,against] I'll keep them out of the kitchen, at least.
[debate,for] Come to the pens at feeding time and tell me they're just livestock.
[argue,for] Go on, call them livestock to their faces.
[argue,against] Sleep in the barn with them, then.

warm.li: [agree] They know who's kind to them, you know.
[debate,against] Even so, be gentle with them.

blunt.li: [argue] Leave the animals out of it.

cheerful.li: [agree,for] I'll give them all a treat and say it's from you.
[debate] Ask the animals, they'd take my side.

gloomy.li: [agree] One hard winter and we'll be eating them anyway.
[debate,against] Don't get attached, it never ends well.

cold.li: [debate] Every animal costs feed, that's the sum of it.
[agree,for] They earn their keep, most of them.

plain.li: [agree,against] I'll find you another blanket.
[agree,for] It's only weather, and it'll pass.
[debate] The sky won't listen to either of us.
[argue,for] Moan at the clouds, then, see if they care.
[argue,against] Easy for you, you never feel the cold.

warm.li: [agree] Stay dry, and come and warm up after.
[debate,for] I'll sew you something warmer, then.

cheerful.li: [agree,for] Whatever it does, I'm going to enjoy it.
[debate] Loser of this one gets the draughty bed.

gloomy.li: [agree,against] It'll be worse before it's better.
[debate] It'll rain on us whatever we think.

cold.li: [debate] Plan for the worst weather and you won't be surprised.
[agree,for] It doesn't change the work.

plain.li: [agree,for] I'll find a spot on the wall for the next piece.
[agree,against] Useful things first, then pretty ones.
[debate] Stand in front of it a while, and then tell me.
[argue,for] Live in a bare box, then.
[argue,against] Eat your sculpture when the stores run low.

warm.li: [agree] Come and look at it with me after supper.
[debate,for] Even you smiled at the last one, I saw you.

cheerful.li: [agree,for] I'll make you something, and you'll have to put it up.
[debate] I'll carve your face next, and then you'll have an opinion.

gloomy.li: [agree,for] It's the only thing here that'll outlast us.
[debate] Pretty or not, it'll be gathering dust within the year.

cold.li: [debate] A fine room lifts people, and people do more work.
[agree,against] Stone has better uses.

plain.li: [agree,for] I'll plant something that takes years to grow, then.
[agree,against] Let's keep our boots by the door, just in case.
[debate] We'll know better once this winter's done with us.
[argue,for] Pack your bag, then, and see how far you get.
[argue,against] Dig your grave here, then, I won't.

warm.li: [agree] Wherever we end up, I want you there.
[debate,for] Stay a while longer, things might turn.

blunt.li: [agree,for] We stay and we dig in.

cheerful.li: [agree,for] In ten years we'll laugh about this.
[debate] I'll still be here, and I'll still be right.

gloomy.li: [agree,against] Nothing here lasts, so why should we?
[debate] Stay or go, the world gets us in the end.

cold.li: [debate] The stores will tell us whether we last.
[agree,for] Then we build for the long haul.

plain.li: [agree,for] I'll put in an hour on it after supper.
[agree,against] Let's bring it up before they pour more into it.
[debate] Finish it first, and then we'll know.
[argue,for] Stand aside, then, and let the rest of us build it.
[argue,against] Break your back for it, then.

warm.li: [agree] Let's work on it side by side tomorrow.
[debate,against] Give it till the season's out, for the ones who care about it.

cheerful.li: [agree,for] We'll scratch our names on it when it's done.
[debate] When it's finished, you'll be the first to brag about it.

gloomy.li: [agree,against] All that work for nothing, mark my words.
[debate,for] It'll get finished just in time for something to ruin it.

cold.li: [debate] We know what it costs, and we don't know what it's worth.
[agree,for] It's worth the materials.

plain.li: [agree,for] I'll go through the stores for anything worth selling.
[agree,against] Full bellies and dry beds, that's rich enough.
[debate] Ask me again when the strongbox is empty.
[argue,for] Hug your principles when the traders won't deal with us.
[argue,against] Count your silver, then, and tell me how warm it keeps you.

warm.li: [agree] Whatever we've got, we've got together.
[debate,for] A bit more put by wouldn't hurt, that's all.

cheerful.li: [agree,for] When we're rich, I'm having a feather bed.
[debate] Rich or poor, I'll still beat you at cards.

gloomy.li: [agree,for] We'll never have enough, not out here.
[debate] Raiders come for the rich ones first.

cold.li: [debate] Wealth draws raiders, and raiders cost lives.
[agree,for] More trade, and fewer gifts.

plain.li: [agree,for] I'll help set the tables on the day.
[agree,against] We'll keep it short and get back to work.
[debate] Come for the start, and if it's dull you can leave.
[argue,for] Work through it, then, and miss the best supper of the season.
[argue,against] Keep your day, I'll keep the stores full.
[agree,sombre] I'll stand with you when it comes.

warm.li: [agree,coming] I've been looking forward to it for weeks.
[debate,for] Come for the supper at least, for me.

cheerful.li: [agree,!sombre] I'm wearing my best shirt, so make an effort.
[debate,for,!sombre] You'll be the first one dancing, I know you.

gloomy.li: [agree] Another day come and gone, and we're still here.
[debate,!sombre] I'll go, but I won't enjoy it.

cold.li: [debate] A day off costs a day of work, that's the only sum.
[agree,for] It keeps people content, so it stays.

plain.li: [agree,for] Next trader through, I'll ask what they need out there.
[agree,against] Let them sort out their own troubles.
[debate] The news is old by the time it reaches us anyway.
[argue,for] Close your eyes to it, then, it'll still be there.
[argue,against] Fix the world, then, after you've fixed your own bed.
[agree,badnews] Poor souls, whoever they are.

warm.li: [agree,goodnews] It's nice to hear people out there are doing well.
[debate,against] Even so, I hope they're all right.

cheerful.li: [agree,for] One day they'll tell stories about us out there.
[debate] I'll get the real story from the next trader, you'll see.

gloomy.li: [agree,badnews] It only ever gets worse out there.
[debate,against] Help them, and they'll forget us the moment it's over.

cold.li: [debate] We act where it profits us, and nowhere else.
[agree,for] A say in the region is worth having.

plain.li: [agree,for] I'll take them some bread in the morning.
[agree,against] I'll walk past their fires once before bed, just to see.
[debate] They're only passing through, give it a few days.
[argue,for] They've done nothing to you but camp.
[argue,against] Make them a bed in your room, then.
[agree,leaving] I'll miss the noise of them when they go.

warm.li: [agree,campfamily] Their little ones looked cold, I'll find a blanket.
[debate,for] They're tired travelers, that's all.

blunt.li: [argue,for] They're not hurting you, so leave off.

cheerful.li: [agree,trader] I'm off to haggle before you get the good stuff.
[debate,for] Wait till you taste their bread, you'll change your tune.

gloomy.li: [agree,tense] If it goes bad, it'll go bad quickly.
[debate] Camps come and go, and so does the trouble.

cold.li: [debate] What they bring is worth more than what they take, so far.
[agree,against] I'll mark where they've set their fires.

plain.li: [agree,for] Next caravan, I'm asking where they've been.
[agree,against] We've all we need inside the wall.
[debate] Depends who's at the gate, doesn't it.
[argue,for] Lock yourself in, then, I'm going to meet them.
[argue,against] Let them all in, then, and count the spoons after.

warm.li: [agree,for] It'd be nice to have friends beyond the wall.
[debate,for] Strangers aren't all bad, you know.

cheerful.li: [agree,for] One day I'll walk to the next town and back, just to see it.
[debate] Let's ask the next visitor and settle it.

gloomy.li: [agree,against] Every stranger's a risk.
[debate] Friends or not, they all leave in the end.

cold.li: [debate] Every visitor is either a trade or a threat.
[agree,for] Trading partners are worth keeping.

plain.li: [agree,child] I'll be back before supper.
[debate,child] Just one more game, then I'll help.
[argue,child] It's not fair, and you know it isn't.
[agree,!child] Off with you, and stay out of the workshop.
[debate,!child,against] Learn this first, then go and play.
[argue,!child,for] The chores will keep, so go and be a child.

warm.li: [agree,child] I love you too.
[agree,!child] You're a good one, you know that?

blunt.li: [argue,child] I'm big enough to help, you said so.

cheerful.li: [agree,child] I'll bring you back the best stone I find!
[debate,!child] Tell you what, I'll race you to the end of the chores.

gloomy.li: [agree,child] I'll grow up anyway, whatever anyone says.
[debate,!child] I was younger than you when I had to work.

cold.li: [debate,child] I can do it myself.
[argue,!child] Questions after chores, not before.

plain.li: [agree,for] I'll save you a place at the next rite.
[agree,against] We'll keep our doubts between ourselves, then.
[debate] Ask me again after a bad winter.
[argue,against] Pray, then, and I'll get on with the work.

warm.li: [debate,against] Whatever you believe, I'm glad you're here.

blunt.li: [argue,for] Mock it if you like, it's still true.

cheerful.li: [debate] If you're right, you can tell me so in the next life.

gloomy.li: [debate,against] Faith or not, the winters are just as long.

cold.li: [agree,against] Belief is a private matter.
